full: The specific radioligand used for this PSMA-PET scan, influencing pharmacokinetic thresholds.

comments.68Ga-PSMA-11: Standard gallium-68 based tracer, renally excreted, low bone false positive rate.
comments.18F-PSMA-1007: Fluorine-18 based tracer, hepatobiliary excretion. Higher rate of unspecific bone uptake (UBU) (~36%) mimicking metastases.
comments.18F-DCFPyL: Fluorine-18 based tracer, renally excreted, standard clinical alternative.

full: What is the specific anatomical descriptor or tracking name for this lesion?

comments.input_guidance: Provide a consistent label (e.g., 'Right Iliac Node 1', 'L4 Vertebra') to track this specific lesion across multiple scans.

full: Primary anatomical site of the lesion in the body, which dictates spread pathway probability and pre-test likelihood.
allowed_answer: Axial Skeleton (Spine, Pelvis, Ribs, Skull, Sternum, Clavicles)
Distant Lymph Node (Common Iliac, Retroperitoneal, Inguinal, Supraclavicular, Axillary)

comments.Prostate Gland: Primary tumor site. Subject to PRIMARY score criteria (zonal location and SUVmax).
comments.Axial Skeleton (Spine, Pelvis, Ribs, Sku: Highly preferred bone metastatic site due to drainage via Batson's valveless venous plexus.
comments.Appendicular Skeleton (Limbs, Scapulae,: Lower probability site for isolated metastasis; typical of widespread disease or benign cartillage/bone mimics (e.g. enchondromas in hands/feet).
comments.Pelvic Lymph Node: Regional N1 nodes located strictly below the common iliac artery bifurcation (e.g., obturator, internal/external iliac, presacral). Pathological size limits: obturator >8 mm, internal iliac >7 mm. Micrometastases can occur in normal-sized nodes.
comments.Distant Lymph Node (Common Iliac, Retrop: Distant M1a nodes located at or above the common iliac bifurcation (common iliac, para-aortic, retroperitoneal, mediastinal, or supraclavicular).
comments.Solid Organ / Viscera: Hematogenous distant metastasis (M1c disease), e.g., liver, lungs, brain, adrenals.
comments.Neural Ganglion / Sympathetic Chain: Common site of false-positive sympathetic/sensory ganglion tracer uptake (e.g. C7, kidney para-aortic).
comments.General Soft Tissue (Muscles, Subcutaneo: Can harbor schwannomas, hemangiomas, or metastases.
comments.Direct Rectal Infiltration: Primary prostate tumor invading the rectal wall through Denonvilliers' fascia (T4 disease).
comments.Direct Bladder Infiltration: Primary prostate tumor invading the bladder neck/detrusor muscle (T4 disease).
comments.Lacrimal Gland: Secretory gland with physiological high tracer accumulation (PSMA-RADS 1).
comments.Salivary Gland: Secretory salivary glands (parotid, submandibular) with intense physiological tracer accumulation (PSMA-RADS 1).
comments.Urinary Bladder: Physiological urinary excretion reservoir. Accumulates high concentration of excreted tracer (PSMA-RADS 1).
comments.Blood Vessel: Vascular structures showing blood pool tracer retention or clearance, mimicking lymphadenopathy (PSMA-RADS 1).

full: Fine-grained compartment within the anatomic location, aiding in distinguishing neoplastic infiltration from physiological uptake or benign mimics.
allowed_answer: Testicular Lymph Node Route (Para-aortic / Renal Hilum)

comments.Medullary Cavity (Intramedullary/Marrow): Prostate bone metastases typically initiate here, replacing red marrow.
comments.Cortical Bone (Intracortical): Benign lesions are often intracortical, unlike metastases which start in marrow.
comments.Juxtacortical / Surface: Surface-based bone formation, typical of benign exostoses or parosteal sarcoma.
comments.Subchondral (Extends to Articular Surfac: Sclerosis strictly subchondral points to joint degeneration.
comments.Metadiaphysis / Metaphysis / Diaphysis: Longitudinal position in long bones. Fibrous dysplasia, enchondromas, and bone cysts prefer metadiaphysis.
comments.Epiphysis: Benign spotted bone disease prefers epiphysis and metaphysis.
comments.Vertebral Endplate: Herniations occur in the center of the endplate.
comments.Prostate Peripheral Zone (PZ): Most common zone for prostate cancer. Focal uptake here is highly suspicious.
comments.Prostate Transition/Central Zone (TZ/CZ): Subject to BPH mimics. Symmetric CZ is physiological; focal TZ >2x background is suspicious.
comments.Prostate Capsule / Apex: Uptake touching capsule/apex increases likelihood of extraprostatic extension.
comments.Intranodal Cortex (Asymmetric Gradient): Classic spatial signature of early micrometastasis seeding via afferent lymphatics.
comments.Lymph Node Hilum: Uptake centered at a preserved fatty hilum favors benign reactive processes.
comments.Liver Lobe: Focal hypoattenuating lesions indicate visceral metastasis.
comments.Pancreatic Tail / Left Upper Quadrant (L: Location of splenules which mimic pancreatic NETs or metastases.
comments.Brain Extra-Axial / Dural-Based: Dural-based extra-axial masses with high PSMA represent a common second primary trap.
comments.Adrenal Cortex: Source of benign adenomas (lipid-rich) vs adrenal metastases.
comments.Anal Canal (Below Levator Ani): Epicenter below levator ani indicates anal cancer, draining to inguinal nodes.
comments.Rectal Ampulla (Above Levator Ani): Epicenter above levator ani indicates rectal cancer, draining to mesorectal/hypogastric nodes.
comments.Thyroid Upper Two-Thirds: Parafollicular C-cell origin site for medullary thyroid cancer.
comments.Unilateral Left Lobe: Primary tumor confined strictly to the left lobe of the prostate (does not cross the midline).
comments.Unilateral Right Lobe: Primary tumor confined strictly to the right lobe of the prostate (does not cross the midline).
comments.Ipsilateral Regional Drainage: Pelvic lymph node located on the same side as the unilateral primary tumor; highly suspicious.
comments.Contralateral Regional Drainage: Pelvic lymph node located on the opposite side of the unilateral primary tumor.
comments.Bladder Wall / Detrusor Muscle: Target of direct anterior infiltration from the prostate base.
comments.Rectal Wall / Muscularis Layer: Target of direct posterior infiltration through the rectoprostatic fat plane.
comments.Anterior Cortex of Tibia: Highly specific cortical sublocation for benign osteofibrous dysplasia or aggressive adamantinoma.
comments.Internal Auditory Canal: Origin site for vestibular schwannoma (eighth cranial nerve), helping differentiate CP angle meningiomas.
comments.Anterior Fibromuscular Stroma (Prostate): Anterior prostate stroma, avascular, focal contour bulge or early enhancement points to cancer.
comments.Testicular Lymph Node Route (Para-aortic: Direct lymphatic route from the testes, bypassing pelvic chains directly to the renal hilum.
comments.N/A (General Organ): Applicable for general organs or clearance sites that do not have sublocation divisions.

full: Internal density and matrix structure evaluated on CT (Hounsfield Units) or contrast dynamics, revealing cellular composition.

comments.Sclerotic / Blastic / Ivory (>1000 HU): Classic prostate cancer osteoblastic metastasis matrix, or benign enostosis. Active metastases present as amorphous, fluffy, cloud-like medullary densities that are T1-hypointense, T2/STIR-hyperintense with post-contrast enhancement and restricted diffusion (dark ADC), often showing a surrounding marrow edema 'halo sign' (unlike enostosis/Paget's which spare marrow). Enostosis has uniform CT density >1000 HU and is T1/T2 hypointense.
comments.Lytic / Lucent (Bone Destruction): Bone-destroying pattern. Metastatic osteolytic clones present with an aggressive permeative or moth-eaten pattern containing numerous <1 mm lucencies, ill-defined margins, and wide zones of transition. Punched-out without rim suggests myeloma.
comments.Mixed Lytic & Sclerotic: Combined bone destruction and formation, typical of mixed metastasis or aggressive tumors.
comments.Central radiolucent nidus (Osteoid Osteo: Small central radiolucent nidus surrounded by dense reactive osteosclerosis. Benign osteoid osteoma signature, typical if age < 40.
comments.Arciform Arterial Enhancement (Accessory: Focal arc-like or centripetal contrast enhancement in arterial phase, pathognomonic for accessory spleen/splenosis.
comments.Adrenal Washout (Absolute >60% / Relativ: Precise CT contrast washout kinetics indicating benign lipid-rich or lipid-poor adrenal adenoma.
comments.Ground-Glass / Fibrous (70-130 HU): Fibro-osseous ground-glass mineralization with diagnostic CT attenuation strictly 70 to 130 HU. Expansile intramedullary lesion, endosteal scalloping with budding appearance on MRI, and coxa vara shepherd's crook bowing deformity (Fibrous Dysplasia).
comments.Fluid-Filled / Cystic (Water Density): True fluid attenuation. Differentiates simple cysts or chronic liquefied hepatic hematomas (0-20 HU) from solid/fibrous ground-glass masses.
comments.Fat Density / Trapped Fat: Preserved fat density. Trapped fat suggests benign hemangioma, Paget's, or lipid-rich adrenal adenoma.
comments.Coarse Trabeculation: Disorganized, thickened trabecular remodeling typical of Paget's.
comments.Corduroy / Polka-Dot Trabeculation: Thickened vertical trabeculae in vertebrae, pathognomonic for spinal hemangioma.
comments.Honeycomb / Swiss Cheese Trabeculation: Multiple rings and arcs of bone mixed with coarse trabeculae in flat or tubular bones.
comments.Chondroid Ring-and-Arc Calcification: Stippled, punctate, flocculent, or classic ring-and-arc matrix calcifications, pathognomonic for enchondroma.
comments.Microcalcifications (Psammomatous): Amorphous granular psammoma bodies, characteristic of papillary thyroid cancer.
comments.Coarse Central Calcification: Coarse stromal calcifications, seen in medullary thyroid cancer, neuroendocrine tumors, or hemangiomas.
comments.Central Necrosis (Low Density): Pathognomonic central hypo-attenuating necrotic core (100% PPV for lymph node metastases; T2 hyperintense, unenhancing center with peripheral ring enhancement).
comments.Gas-Generating / Emphysematous: Gas pockets in tissues or bladder wall, pathognomonic for emphysematous infections.
comments.Uniformly Homogeneous: Solid uniform density without internal variance, characteristic of benign enostosis.
comments.Reticular / Septal Thickening: Linear or network-like interstitial thickening on lung CT, characteristic of pulmonary fibrosis.
comments.Traction Bronchiectasis: Irregular dilatation of bronchi within areas of pulmonary fibrosis due to mechanical traction by surrounding fibrous tissue.
comments.Honeycombing: Clustered cystic air spaces in the lung periphery, diagnostic of advanced pulmonary fibrosis.

full: Outer transition zone and margins of the lesion, reflecting local growth rate and aggressiveness.
allowed_answer: Reactive Sclerotic Rim (Sharp Outer, Fuzzy Inner)

comments.Reactive Sclerotic Rim (Sharp Outer, Fuz: Narrow zone of transition with peripheral sclerosis. Seen in slowly growing or treated bone metastases, osteoid osteomas, or cysts. Therapy-induced sclerotic responses (ADT, chemotherapy, radiation, or bisphosphonates) develop a reactive sclerotic rim progressing centripetally, leading to dense eburnation.
comments.Serpiginous (Snake-like) Margin: Wavy, calcified boundary wrapping around fat, pathognomonic for bone infarction.
comments.Ill-Defined / Permeative / Moth-Eaten Ma: Rapidly growing bone-destroying processes, highly aggressive.
comments.Sharp / Well-Defined (Non-Sclerotic): Punched-out margin without reactive sclerosis, characteristic of myeloma.
comments.Spiculated / Feathered / Thorny (Blendin: Radiating thorny spicules blending into adjacent trabeculae, pathognomonic for bone islands (enostoses). Represents outer margin integrating with host bone without destruction.
comments.Smooth / Well-Defined Margins: Slowly growing benign nodules, normal anatomical variants, or encapsulated tumors.
comments.Incomplete or Absent Halo: Thyroid nodule with incomplete halo indicates infiltration, raising malignancy suspicion.
comments.Complete Halo / Fibrous Capsule: Well-defined fibrous capsule around a thyroid nodule, favoring benignity.
comments.Rind Sign (Thick Sclerotic Reactive Rim): Very thick, smooth sclerotic border in intertrochanteric femur, classic for fibrous dysplasia.
comments.Overhanging Edges (Apple Core): Abrupt shelf-like luminal narrowing edges, classic for colonic adenocarcinoma.
comments.Irregular Extramural Fat Stranding: Stranding in perivesical or pericolic fat indicates stage T3b/T4 local spread (or post-biopsy edema).

full: Morphological shape in three dimensions (3D planes), crucial for distinguishing standard lymph node layouts, ganglia, and bone remodeling.

comments.Spherical: Uniform dimensions in all planes. Can represent primary tumor or focal bone metastasis.
comments.Oval / Bean-Shaped: Normal lymph node shape with a longitudinal-to-short axis ratio (L/T) >= 2. Differentiates normal nodes from spherical metastatic infiltration.
comments.Round: Metastatic lymph nodes lose their elongated shape and round out due to radial tumor growth (L/T ratio < 2), a highly suspicious geometric sign of nodal malignancy.
comments.Teardrop / Comma-Shaped: Maintained in 3D, molds to bone/fascia. Pathognomonic for sympathetic ganglia (resolves oblique slice illusion).
comments.Elongated (Spanning >3 Vertebrae / Paral: Elongated along the long axis of bone (bone island) or spanning vertically in spinal muscle (ganglion).
comments.Wedge-Shaped: Linear, wedge-shaped, or diffuse pattern in prostate (prostatitis) or lung (lobar infection).
comments.Annular / Constricting ('Apple Core'): Constricting collar around lumen with overhanging margins, classic for colon cancer.
comments.Dumbbell Shaped: Mass splayed through neural foramina causing smooth pressure erosion, typical of schwannoma.
comments.Broad-Based / Dural-Based: Dural-based extra-axial mass, classic meningioma location (second primary trap).
comments.Tuberous / Lobulated: Bulky tuberous contours, typical of primary thyroid lymphoma.
comments.Expansile / Ballooning / Blowout: Causes cortical expansion and thinning. ABC has ballooning blowout; FD has smooth expansion.

full: The spatial alignment of the lesion relative to anatomical landmarks (such as the long axis of bone, joints, or vessels).
allowed_answer: Parallel to the Long Axis of Bone

comments.Parallel to the Long Axis of Bone: Classic alignment for benign enostosis; metastases are typically spherical and do not align.
comments.Horizontal: Oriented transversely across bone cortex, typical of traumatic or stress fractures (e.g. atypical femoral fracture).
comments.Vertical: Vertical trabecular reinforcement, typical of corduroy/polka-dot hemangiomas.
comments.Radial / Sunburst: Spicules radiating outwards, typical of Kaposiform infiltrations or osteosarcoma.
comments.Centripetal Enhancement: Contrast enhancement filling from periphery inwards over time, pathognomonic for hemangiomas.
comments.Perilymphatic Distribution: Nodules aligned along bronchovascular bundles and pleural surfaces, classic for sarcoidosis.

full: Multi-lesion spatial distributions or alignment patterns across the scan volume, highly indicative of etiology.
allowed_answer: Linear Alignment Across Ribs ('Pearls on a string')

comments.Linear Alignment Across Ribs ('Pearls on: Uptake points aligned in a row along adjacent ribs, pathognomonic for trauma/fractures.
comments.Bilateral and Symmetric Distribution: Physiologic ganglia, symmetric BPH lobes, symmetric joint arthritis, or bilateral hilar nodes.
comments.Asymmetric / Unilateral Focus: Unilateral or random distribution, highly favors metastatic seeding.
comments.Solitary / Isolated Focus: Single lesion. Clinically evaluated against specific morphological and quantitative criteria.
comments.Multifocal / Polyostotic (>5 foci): Multiple bones/nodes involved, heavily diagnostic of advanced metastatic disease vs spotted bone dysplasia.
comments.Monostotic (Single Bone): Involvement of only one bone. Common in early Paget's (25% of cases) or monostotic fibrous dysplasia.
comments.Scattered / Spotted Sclerosis: Dozens of small, symmetric, uniform bone islands clustered in epiphyses, pathognomonic for osteopoikilosis.

full: The impact of the lesion on the adjacent spongy marrow cavity and fat signals.
short q: Relation to Bone Marrow (Surrounding Changes Part A)

comments.Infiltrative (Replaces Marrow Fat): Obliterates trabeculae and replaces lipid-rich fatty marrow (CT density >40 HU, versus osteoporosis <20 HU). MRI shows T1 hypointensity, STIR hyperintensity, restricted diffusion (dark ADC), and post-contrast enhancement. Highly specific for metastasis/myeloma.
comments.Non-Infiltrative (Spares Marrow Fat): Intact marrow fat. Differentiates benign mimics (like enostosis or severe osteoporosis where fat density is preserved <20 HU) from infiltrative malignant processes.

full: Outer cortical bone reactions, indicative of slow remodeling vs aggressive breakthrough.

comments.None: No periosteal reaction. Characteristic of stable benign entities, simple bone cysts, enchondromas, or early intracancellous metastases.
comments.Diffuse Cortical Expansion (Pagetoid): Widening of the overall bone caliber with cortical splitting/thickening (Paget's). Bowing, insufficiency fractures (Looser zones), preserved T1 fatty marrow signal on MRI (rules out metastasis), and skull mouse-face / calvarium Yarmulke scintigraphy signs.
comments.Thick / Solid Reaction (Callus): Broad, smooth cortical new bone formation, typical of healing fractures, chronic stress reaction, or chronic infections.
comments.Aggressive / Sunburst / Spiculated: Fast-growing spicules of bone forming perpendicular to the cortex, typical of primary osteosarcoma or acute aggressive periostitis.
comments.Codman Triangle: Triangular elevation of periosteum away from cortex, indicating aggressive elevation (sarcoma or acute osteomyelitis).
comments.Local Cortical Hypertrophy / Pressure Er: Localized cortical reactive thickening adjacent to a soft-tissue mass, typical of benign vascular or neurogenic lesions.
comments.Focal/Localized Periosteal Reaction: Focal periosteal reaction adjacent to a bone lesion, indicative of metastatic osseous breakthrough.
comments.Multilamellated / Onion-Skin: Multilamellated concentric layers of new bone, indicating intermediate aggressiveness (Ewing sarcoma, LCH, or acute osteomyelitis).

full: Pathognomonic radiological signs in adjacent soft tissues or bone cortex.
allowed_answer: Vacuum Cleft Sign (Gas in vertebral body)
Blade of Grass / Flame-Shaped Margin (Osteolytic Paget)
Abe Lincoln / Black Beard Sign (Mandible Paget)
short q: Other Structural & Soft Tissue Changes (Surrounding Changes Part C)

comments.Cortical Thinning / Endosteal Scalloping: Gradual erosion of inner cortex by intramedullary pressure, typical of expansile benign cysts, fibrous dysplasia, or enchondromas.
comments.Cortical Breakthrough / Destruction: Erosion through outer cortex, highly suggestive of aggressive malignant infiltration, osteosarcoma, or active osteomyelitis.
comments.Soft-Tissue Edema / Swelling: Localized fluid reaction. For skeletal metastases, this represents the pathognomonic MRI 'halo sign' of hyperintense bone marrow edema or a fluid-filled gap (due to trabecular destruction) surrounding the lesion. Absent in enostosis/Paget's.
comments.Associated Soft-Tissue Mass: Extension of bone tumor into a surrounding soft-tissue component, classic for aggressive metastases or primary sarcomas.
comments.Hematoma-like morphology (Mimic): Mass mimicking a hematoma on CT. If SUVpeak exceeds the Parotid gland, it is highly suspicious for a hemorrhagic or necrotic neoplasm.
comments.Fascicular Sign (Schwannoma MR signature: On MRI, multiple small, round, intermediate-signal structures within a mass, providing a pathognomonic Schwannoma signature.
comments.Beveled Edge Sign / Sequestrum (Calvariu: Pathognomonic CT/skull X-ray signs indicating Eosinophilic Granuloma / Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis.
comments.Dripping Candle Wax (Melorheostosis): Flowing cortical hyperostosis along the cortex resembling melting wax, pathognomonic for Melorheostosis.
comments.Dense Linear Striations (Osteopathia Str: Dense linear striations parallel to the long axis of the bone, pathognomonic for Osteopathia Striata.
comments.Lipohaemarthrosis (Fat-Fluid Level): Marrow fat and blood pooling in joint space (pathognomonic for intra-articular fracture) or gravity-dependent fluid-fluid level (hematocrit effect) due to clotted blood settling in liquefying hepatic hematomas.
comments.Vacuum Cleft Sign (Gas in vertebral body: Linear gas collection within a collapsed vertebra, virtually excludes metastatic disease (pathognomonic for benign osteoporotic fracture).
comments.Puzzle Sign (Cortical fragment alignment: Fracture fragments fit together perfectly like puzzle pieces, indicating no bone resorption or tumor mass.
comments.Fallen Fragment Sign: Cortical fragment settles to the bottom of a fluid-filled cavity, pathognomonic for simple bone cyst.
comments.Dural Tail Sign (Tapering enhancement): Tapering, enhancing dural tail adjacent to a broad dural mass, highly specific for meningioma.
comments.Local Tissue Infiltration (Trachea/Esoph: Infiltration of anterior neck structures, typical of aggressive thyroid cancers.
comments.Perivesical Fat Stranding / Haziness: Fat stranding adjacent to bladder wall. Indicates T3b extravesical spread or post-biopsy edema.
comments.Soap-Bubble Appearance (Pseudotrabeculat: Concentric internal bony ridges in thinned/expanded cortex, typical of GCT, ABC, NOF, desmoplastic fibroma, or plasmacytoma.
comments.Blowout Appearance (Highly Expansile): Explosive osteolytic expansion, highly suggestive of hypervascular metastasis (renal or thyroid) or Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism.
comments.Nodular Septal Enhancement (Malignant se: Solid nodular enhancement along internal septa, differentiating telangiectatic osteosarcoma from simple/aneurysmal bone cysts.
comments.Vascularized Nidus with CT/MRI Groove: Central highly vascularized nidus with a feeding vessel groove on CT, pathognomonic for osteoid osteoma.
comments.Blade of Grass / Flame-Shaped Margin (Os: A sharply demarcated wedge-shaped resorption zone, pathognomonic for the early active osteolytic phase of Paget's disease.
comments.Yarmulke Sign (Skull Paget): Diffuse skull vault expansion with calvarial thickening, mimicking a skullcap, classic for Paget's disease.
comments.Abe Lincoln / Black Beard Sign (Mandible: Intense symmetric uptake throughout the mandible, pathognomonic for mandibular Paget's disease.
comments.Architectural Distortion: Disruption of the normal alignment or spacing of lung parenchyma or surrounding structures, seen in chronic pulmonary processes or severe fibrosis.

full: Standardized Uptake Value (SUV) metrics and comparisons to reference organs, acting as quantitative gates in the decision tree.

comments.SUVpeak > Blood Pool SUVmean (PSMA Avid): Basic gate for PSMA avidity. If true, lesion is considered PSMA-avid. If false, lesion is PSMA-cold.
comments.SUVpeak > Spleen SUVmean: Used to confirm bone metastasis in cases of equivocal CT morphology or multifocal lesions without CT correlates.
comments.SUVmax > 12 (Definite Primary): Primary prostate peripheral zone focal uptake gate. If true, indicates definite clinically significant cancer (PRIMARY 5).
comments.TZ Uptake > 2x Background Transition Zon: Primary prostate transition zone focal uptake gate. Differentiates malignant TZ tumors (PRIMARY 3) from BPH nodules (PRIMARY 2).
comments.18F-PSMA-1007 Bone Lesion with SUV < 10: Specific check for 18F-PSMA-1007 tracer. Isolated bone lesions with SUV < 10 have an intrinsic 51.4% false positive rate; requires conservative scoring.
comments.Unspecified Bone Uptake (UBU): Low-grade bone uptake without clear CT correlate or clinical context correlation. Biopsy should be avoided unless other metastatic indicators are present.

full: Patient demographic data, treatment status, and tumor biology history which adjust diagnostic probability.
allowed_answer: Patient Age < 40 Years Old (Out of Scope)
Recent COVID-19 / Viral Pneumonia (Lung uptake trap)

comments.Patient Age < 40 Years Old (Out of Scope: Prostate cancer is extremely rare. Sclerotic bone lesions in young patients are typically other primaries or congenital conditions.
comments.Patient Age >= 40 Years Old: Standard target demographic. Bone lesions are suspicious for metastasis, myeloma, or Paget's.
comments.Gleason Score 6 (ISUP 1): Grade Group 1: Clinically insignificant or low-grade prostate cancer.
comments.Gleason Score 7 (ISUP 2/3): Grade Group 2 or 3: Intermediate-grade prostate cancer.
comments.Gleason Score 8 (ISUP 4): Grade Group 4: High-grade prostate cancer with significant metastatic risk.
comments.Gleason Score 9-10 (ISUP 5): Grade Group 5: Very high-grade prostate cancer with extremely high risk of aggressive metastasis.
comments.Serum PSA > 20 ng/mL: Elevated PSA, strongly correlated with active lymphatic and skeletal metastasis.
comments.Recent Treatment (<2mo post-radiation/su: Causes inflammatory flare, which can mimic active progression. Requires clinical correlation.
comments.Heavily Pre-treated (Advanced ADT / Chem: Suspect neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) conversion in cold lesions (receptors mutated/lost; FDG-PET recommended).
comments.Original Primary Tumor was PSMA-Cold (~1: If true, cold lesions are highly concordant for true prostate cancer metastases despite lack of avidity.
comments.Previously Treated Lesion (Irradiated /: Lesion was previously a definitive metastasis but has been treated. Maintains a PSMA-RADS 5T score regardless of current uptake.
comments.Widespread Disease (>5 malignant finding: Patient has numerous distinct malignant findings, significantly increasing the pre-test probability that any equivocal lesion is malignant.
comments.Post-Splenectomy Status: Patient had spleen removed. Routes quantitative spleen reference checks to alternative organs to prevent referencing errors.
comments.Recent COVID-19 / Viral Pneumonia (Lung: Causes transient, non-specific ground-glass lung uptake on PSMA-PET mimicking pulmonary spread.
comments.Short PSA Doubling Time (PSADT < 6 month: Aggressive PSA doubling kinetics, strongly increasing the likelihood of true active metastatic disease.
comments.History of Hyperparathyroidism (Brown Tu: Elevates risk of hypervascular lytic en-osteolytic lesions matching Brown Tumors.
comments.NEPC Phenotype (AR-negative / FDG-active: Loss of Androgen Receptor and high glycolytic activity in mCRPC setting. Explains cold PSMA-RADS 3D lesions.
comments.High Genomic Risk (Decipher/Oncotype/Pro: High genetic risk of cell-cycle progression or adverse pathology, increasing suspicion for primary or metastatic PCa.
comments.Has >5 Other PSMA-Avid Metastases: Indicates tumor heterogeneity. An isolated cold lesion is likely a metastasis clone that lost PSMA expression.
comments.High Tumor Burden (>=5 Metastases): Presence of 5 or more metastases across the scan, representing high general risk and systemic progression.
comments.Low Tumor Burden (<5 Metastases): Less than 5 metastases, indicating oligometastatic or early disease where false-positive rules in atypical sites apply.

full: Maximum SUV value in this lesion
Automatically calculated PRIMARY score (v1.0) based on zonal location and SUVmax.

comments.PRIMARY 1 (No Pattern): Very Low Risk. No dominant pattern, or overridden by physiological/edge artifacts.
comments.PRIMARY 2 (Diffuse TZ / Symmetric CZ): Low Risk. Diffuse Transitional Zone or Symmetric Central Zone uptake.
comments.PRIMARY 3 (Focal TZ): Intermediate Risk. Focal Transition Zone uptake > 2x Background TZ.
comments.PRIMARY 4 (Focal PZ): High Risk. Focal Peripheral Zone uptake.
comments.PRIMARY 5 (SUVmax >= 12): Very High Risk. Intense focal uptake with SUVmax > 12.

full: Automatically calculated PSMA-RADS v2.0 score based on location, SUV, and morphology.

comments.PSMA-RADS 1: Definitively Benign. Pathognomonic mimics (e.g., Ganglion, Hemangioma, Bone Island, Osteoarthritis) or physiological clearance.
comments.PSMA-RADS 2: Likely Benign. Equivocal/Low uptake in an Atypical anatomical site, or sympathetic ganglion.
comments.PSMA-RADS 3A: Indeterminate soft tissue/node. Equivocal/Low uptake in a typical soft tissue or nodal location.
comments.PSMA-RADS 3B: Indeterminate bone. Equivocal/Low uptake in a typical bone location.
comments.PSMA-RADS 3C: Intense atypical. Intense uptake in an Atypical site; requires clinical workup to rule out a 2nd malignancy.
comments.PSMA-RADS 3D: Suspicious unavid lesion. No significant uptake but structural mass or cortical gap is highly suspicious.
comments.PSMA-RADS 4: Highly Likely PCa. Intense uptake in a Typical site but lacking definitive CT structural correlates.
comments.PSMA-RADS 5: Almost Certainly PCa. Intense uptake in a Typical site with definitive CT correlates (enlarged node, sclerotic bone).
comments.PSMA-RADS 5T: Treated Metastasis. Prior therapy (ADT, chemo, radiation, or bisphosphonates) produces a centripetal sclerotic response. Successfully healed/inactive lesions present as cold PSMA bone scars mimicking enostoses, whereas active/recurrent lesions exhibit high uptake.

full: Inferred alternative diagnosis or benign mimic based on morphological and clinical criteria.
Degree of diagnostic certainty (1 = very low, 10 = very high)
Additional clinical comments or observations.
